food.name: Salmon

identity.basisReason: Raw per-100g edible-flesh basis keeps the entry aligned with a base whole-food ingredient rather than a cooked preparation.

scoreReadiness.summary: Strong enough for launch scripting as a raw salmon baseline, but a few protein-quality style fields are still legacy calibration proxies and salmon source variation can move the fat profile.
blockers: wild-versus-farmed and species variation can shift the exact fat and omega-3 profile meaningfully
caveats: Real foods vary by cultivar, brand, season, and preparation; this record is a canonical comparison entry rather than a guarantee for every product.

sourceNotes: All displayed nutrition values are stored and checked on a per-100g basis.
Primary and cross-check nutrition references are listed in nutritionDataSources.
Contextual GI and protein-quality fields are optional when not canonical nutrient facts.

sections.title: Fats
sections.narration: 13 grams of fat. Omega 3 is 2200 milligrams, supporting a more useful fat profile. Saturated fat is 3.1 grams, supporting a cleaner fat profile, but it is the smaller helper in this section. For meats, fat quality is the main tradeoff.

sections.title: Proteins
sections.narration: 20.4 grams of protein. Essential amino acids score is 9 out of 9, making the protein useful for repair and maintenance. Collagen is only 0.3 grams, not adding much structural protein, so for meats, that collagen side of the protein score stays weak. For meats, protein quality matters a lot.

sections.title: Vitamins
sections.narration: Vitamin B12 is 117% daily value, useful for nerve and blood-cell support. Vitamin D is 66% daily value, useful for bone and immune support, but it is not the standout here, so that's a small downside for meats. For meats, vitamin B12 and vitamin D matter most.

sections.title: Minerals
sections.narration: Potassium is 8% daily value, the best number here but still too low to carry this section. Iron is only 4% daily value, not bringing much oxygen-transport support. For meats, iron and zinc can add real value.

sections.title: Pros
sections.narration: The upsides first: easy to build a strong meal around. It works as a genuine centrepiece instead of needing lots of nutritional excuses. Helps make meals feel complete. That practical meal role matters beyond the score rows. Has unusually strong trust with viewers. People already read it as a serious healthy-food choice, which matches its overall case.
